articles.summary: ATLANTA — Donald Trump carved his path to reelection through Georgia, and less than two years into his term, Keisha Lance Bottoms told a crowd here that the president’s policies haven’t just raised prices, “he’s also raised blood pressure.” “Just yesterday, I met with a woman in Tifton who owns a mortuary, and she told me that even the prices of caskets have gone up,” Bottoms said to a roaring crowd on Saturday at the Cobb Convention Center. “Donald Trump is wreaking havoc for the living and the dead.” Bottoms is locked in a tight race to be the next governor of Georgia, running on promises to take on rising costs as a mom with a working-class background and generations of Georgia roots. Rarely does she talk about the fact that if she wins, Bottoms would become the first Black woman ever elected governor in United States history. But it’s a milestone that resonates with many voters, especially Black women who say that it would send a message about the direction of their state and their country. Eva Johnson, 80, traveled an hour to Bottoms’ Atlanta rally. She said Bottoms’ urgency when she talks about the economy reflects her own. “What are we going to do? How are we going to live?”

The S&P 500 fell 1.2% for its worst day since July, while the Nasdaq composite tumbled 2.6%. The weakness for tech stocks was so overwhelming that it masked strength for the rest of the US market, in which the majority of stocks actually rose.
